task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer about South Nacre School District's laptop bids, answering why the lowest upfront figure is not the whole buy-versus-lease decision.

facts.text: South Nacre School District published purchase and lease bids for 300 student laptops in August 2026 and plans a board decision in September.
The purchase bid is $450 per laptop, or $135,000 for 300 devices, paid at delivery.
The lease bid is $54,000 a year for three years, totaling $162,000 before optional charges.
The lease includes ordinary fault repairs and battery replacement when tested capacity falls below its stated threshold.
Accidental damage and missing devices are excluded from that repair coverage.
District technicians estimate purchased-device maintenance at $12,000 annually, or $36,000 over three years, but that is an estimate rather than a fixed vendor price.
Adding the maintenance estimate to the purchase bid gives a three-year comparison of $171,000.
Purchased laptops remain district property after three years; leased laptops must be returned unless the district exercises an option.
The end-of-lease purchase option is $90 per device, adding $27,000 if exercised for all 300.
The district needs 260 regularly assigned devices and plans to keep 40 as repair and enrollment spares.
Its current fleet is six years old and required 71 battery replacements in the 2025–26 school year.
The old fleet's device count and repeat-repair count are not supplied, and its repair history does not establish a failure rate for the new models.
Finance director Sora Brill says the lease would spread cash payments while the purchase would use more of the current capital allocation.
Brill said, "A lower bill in September can come with a different decision waiting three years later."
Technician Peren Moss said staff time arranging repairs and preparing loan devices is not eliminated by either bid.
Moss said, "Someone still has to get a working machine onto the student's desk."
Both bids cover the same specified hardware model and include initial setup, so those items are not differences in this comparison.
Neither bid includes the district's separately purchased teaching-software subscriptions.
The district operates two secondary schools and a shared technology workshop.
The board has not selected a bid or released a reliable resale-value estimate for purchased laptops after three years.

Ownership included automatically in the $162,000 lease or coverage of all accidental damage
